title: How is text/event-stream checked?
body:
Spinning off from https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/7553/files#r808234276

The spec [currently says](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#sse-processing-model)

> HTTP 200 OK responses with a `[Content-Type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#content-type)` header specifying the type `[text/event-stream](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#text/event-stream)`, ignoring any [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) parameters, must be processed line by line [as described below](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#event-stream-interpretation).
>
> HTTP 200 OK responses that have a [Content-Type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#content-type) specifying an unsupported type, or that have no [Content-Type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/b3a49bcf51d5cf39f6233b752f631940a44677ab/#content-type) at all, must cause the user agent to fail the connection.

The exact phrasing will move around a bit as part of #7553 but we're decided not to try to make it more rigorous yet. So:

What about `text/EVENT-stream`? What about multiple `Content-Type` headers? What about whitespace?

The proper architecture here is to use https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type and compare the essences. We should do that. But we should also write web platform tests for the weird cases, as part of that work.
